label: Aurora

county_election_office.name: Arapahoe County Elections (most of Aurora); Adams County Elections (north Aurora); Douglas County Elections (far southeast Aurora). Your ballot comes from the county you live in.
county_election_office.phone: Arapahoe Clerk and Recorder 303-795-4200; Adams County Elections 720-523-6500; Douglas County Elections 303-660-7444

zip_caveats: Aurora spans three counties, and your county decides which county races and judges you see: most of Aurora is in Arapahoe County, north Aurora (roughly north of Colfax) is in Adams County, and a small far-southeast slice is in Douglas County. ZIPs 80010, 80011, 80019, 80045 and parts of 80012 and 80017 straddle the Arapahoe and Adams line; 80016 and 80015 reach into Douglas County near Southlands; 80247 is split between Aurora and Denver; 80014 and 80231 include unincorporated Arapahoe and Denver pockets. All of Aurora is in Congressional District 6 (Census district maps, checked Oct 17). State Senate: District 27 (south Aurora, roughly south of Hampden Ave, plus the Douglas County part) and District 29 (west-central Aurora, roughly between Hampden and 6th Ave west of Buckley Rd) have races this year; most of north and east Aurora, including all of the Adams County part, is in District 28, which has no Senate race in 2026. State House is split among Districts 36 (north and east, including Adams County), 42 (northwest), 41 (west-central), 40 (south-central), 61 (south and southeast), 37 and 56 (small southern pieces) and a sliver of 3 on the western edge. RTD: only the Adams County part of Aurora is in RTD District B, which has an election; the rest of Aurora is in RTD districts with no race this year. Arapahoe commissioners are elected by district, and only Districts 2 and 4 are up, so many Arapahoe County Aurora voters have no commissioner race. Aurora's city measures 3A to 3D appear on every Aurora ballot regardless of county. Front Range rail 7A: Aurora is not in the rail district, but Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas ballots wrongly printed 7A for many voters; state guidance is to vote your ballot as is and clerks will set aside ineligible 7A votes.
